summary: This article explains how igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks form and slowly change from one type into another in the never-ending rock cycle.
introduce: Read the title “The Rock Cycle” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: formed when hot, melted rock cools and hardens
formed from layers of sand, mud, or shells pressed together over time
formed when heat and pressure change one kind of rock into another

challengeTerms.def: the slow breaking down of rock by wind, water, ice, and changes in temperature
the force of something pressing on something else
a solid with a regular shape made of tiny parts arranged in a pattern

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that rocks are one thing in nature that never really changes? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Imagine you are a grain of sand. Describe your journey through the rock cycle.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic, and let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses weathering, pressure, and crystal to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
